supersession_reason: A deeper registry pass found Linear A v2.32 as CURRENT_CANONICAL_RESEARCH_STATE and a newer exact historical-source receipt. v0.1 is preserved as discovery history but is not current authority.
purpose: Reuse already-built JANUS safeguards from Linear A and Egyptian-record work as mandatory prescore canaries for the sacred-text pipeline. These corpora are method controls, not additional witnesses for the Flood hypothesis.

upstream.note: The repository is linked into JANUS Habitat in reference-and-handoff-only mode; source history remains authoritative and no execution authority is implied.

historical_older_same_corpus_baseline_pr.note: Preserved because earlier JANUS stages were frozen against this source state; it does not replace v2.32 current authority.

canaries.historical_case: A strong pre-filter *900 survivor was revealed as Aegean word-separator punctuation.
canaries.topa_test: Punctuation/numeric/format markers injected into anonymized sacred-text packets must receive zero semantic evidence and must not form rare bundles.

canaries.historical_case: v2.32 preserves a strong KU-RO terminal-numeric-payload internal signal but refuses admission because exchangeable target support is 8 while the frozen floor is 10.
canaries.topa_test: A high similarity statistic or low null probability must not unlock Flood promotion when preregistered support/control minima fail.

lexical_canary.topa_test: Keep all three identities distinct unless an independently evidenced relation is supplied. Orthographic/phonetic resemblance alone must not create equivalence.

text_id_canary.topa_test: Shuffle utterance and section numbers as distractors. Numeric coincidence must never generate semantic evidence.

mendes_provenance_canary.rule: A printed/OCR-corrupted hieroglyphic gap remains UNKNOWN even when context makes reconstruction tempting.
mendes_provenance_canary.example: The lower protected gold sheet has two vertical inscription lines confirmed, but exact hieroglyphs/translation remain open; CG 53469 surface inscription remains not established.

possible_flood_negative_control.reason: Wasserman 2020 states that no mention of a great Flood is found in ancient Egyptian literature. This makes Egyptian literature potentially useful as an ancient-culture negative control, but the claim must be independently checked against a defined Egyptian corpus before admission.
possible_flood_negative_control.do_not_do: Do not reinterpret Destruction of Mankind, Nile hymns, Nun/cosmogony or other Egyptian water/destruction texts into a Flood witness merely to fill the slot.
